newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks rise on hopes of early share tax move.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks rise on hopes of early share tax move.

text.p: Japanese stocks perked up on Wednesday, helped by expectations that the government will pursue a swift review of taxes on securities transactions.
The market's key Nikkei index rose more than 500 points in morning trade. The market has sagged in recent sessions on fears that the economy may be set to weaken.

The market had started out strongly, after falling on Tuesday, helped by a rally in Nikkei futures in Chicago overnight. The Nikkei average of 225 leading shares ended the morning session up 511.87 points, or 2.95 percent, at 17,870.03.

The rise was fuelled by comments by key policy makers about a review of a securities transaction tax which brokers complain is dampening stock trade. Brokers have been looking for action from the government to halt the market's recent downward spiral.
"The market was cheered, as the government finally appears to be trying to tackle the securities transaction tax," said a trader at a second-tier Japanese brokerage firm.
A senior Ministry of Finance (MOF) official was quoted by a Japanese newspaper on Wednesday as saying the ministry would likely reach a conclusion on how to revamp the tax by June.
Separately, a senior official of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) party was quoted by another newspaper as saying the LDP is seeking to abolish the tax as early as 1998.
